title: SOC Incident Severity and Response Authority Standard (Sentinel Managed Security)
content:
The security operations center handles Sentinel Managed Security incidents under the following standard. An incident is opened from correlated alerts with a severity, acknowledged by an analyst who begins triage, and closed with any incident response time logged.

## S1 Severity

The SOC assigns severity at detection:

| Severity | Assigned for |
|---|---|
| Critical | Active ransomware, confirmed data exfiltration or domain-admin compromise |
| High | A confirmed compromised host or account |
| Medium | Suspicious activity needing client confirmation |
| Low | Policy violations and informational findings |

## S2 Acknowledgement

Acknowledgement targets are the tier's critical, high, medium and low acknowledgement figures, on a clock running 24 hours a day, seven days a week. A value of 0 means the tier has no human triage (its service description shows no around-the-clock SOC triage) and alerts are delivered to the client by email only. The tier's critical containment target is an objective, not a guarantee.

## S3 Containment authority

The SOC isolates a host without first reaching the client only where host isolation is pre-authorized on the tier, and disables an account only where account disabling is pre-authorized on the tier; otherwise it calls the authorized contact first.

| Action | Pre-authorized on the tier | Not pre-authorized on the tier |
|---|---|---|
| Isolating a compromised host | The SOC may isolate without first reaching the client | The SOC calls the authorized contact first |
| Disabling a compromised user account | The SOC may disable without first reaching the client | The SOC calls the authorized contact first |

## S4 Entitlements

Threat hunting, identity threat detection, email security, dark web monitoring, vulnerability scanning, phishing simulations, security posture reviews, the named security analyst, log retention, the cyber insurance attestation letter and the ransomware warranty pass-through are entitlements of the tier and are never billed per incident.

## S5 Incident response engagement

Incident response engagement is requested by the authorized contact or declared by the SOC on a critical incident, with responders engaged within the tier's engagement target, which is a target. On closure the incident response time is rounded up to the tier's billing increment and is never less than the tier's minimum hours per incident.

### Logged time, illustrated (hypothetical increments and minimums)

| Time worked | Billing increment | Minimum per incident | Rounded up | Hours logged |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 95 minutes | 30 minutes | 2 hours | 120 minutes | 2 |
| 170 minutes | 30 minutes | 2 hours | 180 minutes | 3 |
| 20 minutes | 15 minutes | 1 hour | 30 minutes | 1 (the minimum) |
| 61 minutes | 60 minutes | 4 hours | 120 minutes | 4 (the minimum) |

## Questions the standard answers

**Who may start incident response engagement?** The authorized contact, by request, or the SOC, by declaring it on a critical incident.

**Is a phishing simulation or a posture review charged when it relates to an incident?** No. These are entitlements of the tier and are never billed per incident.
